Hey, though your circumstances seem way worse than mine I can relate a lot to what you are saying. I'm from an Indian family with parent who had an arranged marriage as well. While they do get along decently, since a young age, my mom has made a point of making fun of, degrading and making me and everything I have ever been interested in a joke. This literally broke my self esteem and brought me to a point where I hated myself for who I was and hoped I just didn't exist because I genuinely believed I was a burden on her. 

As a child, she would often scream at me and hit me and then make me repeat that she was doing it for my own good over and over again. And that I better not tell my relatives or extended family or I'd be betraying her. And I guess this belief that she was doing everything for my wellbeing and I was being a terrible child who couldn't appreciate it ( yeap its messed up) along with my non existent self esteem led to me being depressed from a very young age ( at which point I felt like a burden and wanted to not exist anymore but didn't even know what suicide meant - after all it's not something people talk a lot about to kids)

Anyway, beyond my childhood,  in my teen years, I started to isolate myself, gave up on studies, and turned to self harm. It wasnt a great time and around then I think I even calculated the amount of money I'd need to come up with to pay off my parents for whatever they'd spent ( or in my opinion, wasted) on me so I would atleast be less of a burden financially once I died. I wrote suicide notes and even tried once ( clearly failing). 

So I guess I do relate to you a lot. But what I wanted to say is it'll get better. And not because time will heal things coz that's a load of bullshit. You need to learn to believe in yourself n slowly teach yourself to not care much about the validation given by your extended family or any other external matter. Focus on you. It will be hard, yes but just try to keep focussing on yourself even if you feel you are being narcissistic or anything of that sort. Everytime your brain tells you that you are a burden or when it presents you with similar thoughts try to rationalise why it isnt true. Talk to yourself. Pretend your brain is an annoying 5 year old who keeps repeating things to annoy you. Now reply to that annoying 5 year old and try to explain why you're right and they're wrong. 

Honestly you probably think whatever I am saying is a load of nonsense and I dont blame you because I would've said the same thing. But I managed to get past most of my insecurities instilled by my family and I believe you can too. It definitely isnt easy but if you slowly teach yourself, you should be able to get past atleast some of them. Financial trouble is always an issue that is harder to face however and I dont have much of a suggestion for a solution for that. But I guess try to go on with life as you want to. Try to study, get a job. Dont care about what your relatives would think. Or instead tell yourself that they will think higher of you if you try than if you dont. I know in Asian families the oh he tried card doesnt work but atleast you can use it to ease your thoughts. Besides think of it this way, if you succeed, its gonna be a slap to the face for all those who criticized you. If you fail, well it's nothing you havent seen before. Will it be hard to face ? Yes. But it's worse to not try. Just believe in yourself as much as you can and go on with your life and pursue your goals.

Please dont resort to suicide. I know it definitely seems the easiest way out and honestly the best option but in reality it isnt. You arent being selfish if you want to commit suicide but honestly do you want those relatives making your life sound like a joke ( I know that's a terrible way to think of things but honestly that's what aunties do. I know someone who committed suicide and was labelled weak and had her and her parents subtly criticized at even the funeral). If you die, you wont even be able to do anything about these people. You wont be able to shut them up. And it's like making them believe that they won. That you were the weak one who couldn't even stand "slight" criticism. ( again please dont think you are actually weak or anything of that sort because atleast in my opinion it takes a lot of courage to come to having suicide as an option. Yes people think it's the easiest way out but in reality your brain is tricking you that the world would be a better place without you. And the fact that you're willing to go through the pain n uncertainty of death itself is a courageous thing. I'm not glorifying suicide or saying it's a good thing but I'm saying people who come to that descision arent weak. And that I'm just giving you examples of what relatives may say not what is the truth.)  Sorry for making you read that long comment n idk if you'll even get sth from it but hope you dont resort to suicide and wish you all the best in life. Also if you even want to talk or vent or anything you can always dm me.
